# Scheduled routines registry

### Scheduled routines: the registry, because they are invisible from other repos

Adam runs **cloud routines** (claude.ai "Routines", CCR sessions on a schedule)
as well as per-repo CI. They are shared state between agents, and nothing makes
them discoverable: a session in one repo cannot see a routine whose prompt and
playbook live in another, so it will search, find nothing, and reasonably
conclude none exists. That happened on 2026-08-31, which is why this table is
here rather than only in the owning repo's `AGENTS.md`.

**Local scheduled tasks (the Claude desktop app on Adam's machine) are a second
class of routine, and they are the ONLY ones that can drive his Chrome.** They
live in `C:/Users/adamm/.claude/scheduled-tasks/<id>/SKILL.md`, run while the
app is open (a missed one runs at next launch), and are listed with the
`scheduled-tasks` MCP, not `RemoteTrigger`. A cloud playbook that says "local
half only, needs his Chrome, a cloud run says so and stops" describes work
that DOES NOT HAPPEN unless one of these exists for it: seamless's daily-sweep
Check 12 (LinkedIn acceptances, replies, the week's connection requests) sat unrun
for two days that way until 2026-09-18 (Adam: *"wasn't that something you are
to look for every morning?"*). When you write a check that needs Chrome,
create the local task in the same pass.

**Every routine spawns in bypass permissions, every time.** Adam, 2026-09-21,
with two morning routines sitting on an Allow prompt for their first Bash
call: *"the agent spawns on manual every time even when i adjust it and i want
bypass permissions. can you do this and make it stay that way"*, then
*"remember that i want all routine spawns to be bypass permissions. every
time."* A routine nobody is watching that stops on a permission card has done
nothing, and the card is the whole failure. The task definition has no
permission field and the app's mode picker is per session, so the durable
setting is `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in
`C:/Users/adamm/.claude/settings.json` (the user tier, so it reaches a routine
whatever repo it runs from); set there 2026-09-21 and read back through
`ccd_settings get_settings` as `default_permission_mode: bypassPermissions`.
If a routine's run ever shows "Manual" again, that file has lost the key: put
it back, and switch the run already in progress with
`mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_permission_mode` (its session id is in
`list_task_runs`), which applies to the turn it has in flight.

**A business routine that runs more than once a day runs on Sonnet.** Adam,
2026-09-21, on the LinkedIn acceptances task an hour after it went in hourly on
Opus: *"let's have this run every 2 hours but put it on sonnet. everything for
business that's more than once a day is sonnet."* So `fathom-sweep` (hourly)
and `linkedin-acceptances` (every two hours) carry `model: sonnet` in the
frontmatter of their `SKILL.md`, and any new Ramsgate or MudLabs task that
fires more than once a day gets the same line when it is created. Once-a-day
tasks (the morning task, the call confirmations) stay on the default model. Verify it took on the next run (`list_task_runs`, then
`mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__get_session` on the run's session id reports `model`);
a run that still shows Opus is switched in flight with
`mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__set_session_model`, and the frontmatter is not the
mechanism, so say so here. The cadence itself is his read on the same trade:
a check every two hours catches an acceptance within the afternoon, and a
window wider than the cadence (26 hours on acceptances) with a per-person
"already has a card" check is what makes a run cheap to repeat.

Trigger ids live in the owning repo's `AGENTS.md`, next to what each sweep
currently checks. **List them for yourself rather than trusting this table**:
`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger`, then `{action: "list"}`. That is the ground
truth and it takes one call; a hand-written table in a synced file is exactly the
kind of thing that drifts.

**Before building a scheduled check, run that list.** If a sweep already covers
the cadence you need, add a numbered section to its playbook and push instead of
creating a second routine. Two routines reporting the same status is the outcome
this registry exists to prevent.

**Three things do NOT belong in a shared sweep**, and each has a better home:

- **Anything needing a browser.** A cloud routine has no access to Adam's
  Chrome, so a check that drives a console (a Firebase project page, a dashboard
  that will not render headless) can only run locally, and only while that app
  is open.
- **Anything wanting a repo the sweep does not have.** A routine attaches
  specific repos. Adding a check that needs another repo's scripts means
  attaching it, which is a real change to what that routine can read.
- **Anything that might find nothing, when it costs tokens to look.** Adam, 2026-09-25, when a reply he had already read sent no email and a polling run was proposed as the net: *"i don't want anything set up that will use tokens and potentially not find anything."* A wake-up is an event that costs nothing while idle (a mail row, a webhook, a database write); a gap that only a paid poll could close waits for a run that already happens, and the report says so.
- **Anything that needs no judgment at all.** A check that only asks "is this
  queue empty" or "did this value change" should not start a Claude session,
  which pays the whole handbook (300k+ tokens) to learn nothing happened. Put
  it on something already running: a PocketBase hook that fires on the write
  itself (best, since it costs nothing on an empty queue), or a few lines in
  the `semester` Worker's existing `*/15` scheduled handler. **Not a new
  scheduled GitHub Actions workflow**: the 2,000 min/month Actions pool is
  shared by every repo, every run bills at least a minute, free-tier schedules
  fire at roughly 10% of their cadence, and the account ran it dry on
  2026-07-26 (`playbooks/self-hosted-pocketbase.md`). Actions is right only for
  work that already runs in that repo's CI on push. Reach for a cloud routine
  when the work needs judgment or a report written for a human.

The full strategy, including how to add a check without breaking the others, is
`playbooks/agent-sweeps.md`. Add `"agent-sweeps"` to a repo's `playbooks` list in
`repos.json` when that repo starts running one.
